description:
Approved by the user 2026-11-17 (relayed by Bugs and Cleanup, verbatim: ".31 approved."; decision B of the fz-9x7.31 page /Users/j5n/Workspace/fz-9x7.31.html, ordered C: fz-9x7.31 (A) first, then this).

Bug: on the native paths a branch whose join is reached after the branch builds a continuation even when the branch ends in a tail position. `(if n > 5, do: n * 3, else: n) + 1` allocates one 32 B continuation per execution on run and none on interp. A join is reached by a jump (a tail transfer to the join block); only a non-tail call builds a continuation.

Probes: /Users/j5n/Workspace/fz-9x7.31-probes/shapes/ (t_ifjoin.fz, t_try_noarg.fz).

Why it matters: JSON's loop (fz-nml.25) reaches one continuation per iteration only with both fz-9x7.31 and this.

Related design: Make Distiller Fast's byte-walk page (../fz-sc8.byte-walk-loop.html, with the user) proposes clause bodies as blocks of their function and a self tail call as a jump under the same rule ("an entry reached only by its function's own direct transfers is a block"); the builder reads that page first so the two land as one design, not two mechanisms.

Acceptance: the probe allocates no continuation on run/build; interp, JIT and AOT agree; pins that fall are lowered, none rises.
title: A branch join is reached by a tail call; only a non-tail call builds a continuation
